title: Benchmarks for Hard Grounded Research
paper_question: What tasks actually make grounded research hard, beyond simple fact lookup?
categories: citation supports fact but not conclusion
temporal questions: as of date X

approaches.name: Reuse existing QA and evidence labels
approaches.description: Convert native dataset questions, answers, evidence spans, tables, and unanswerable labels into grounded research QA items.
strengths: Fastest path to a working public benchmark.
risks: Native labels often reward answer extraction rather than research judgment.
Some failure modes need synthetic perturbations.

approaches.name: Adversarially transform existing rows
approaches.description: Inject stale/current snapshots, distractor authority conflicts, appended updates, and conclusion-overreach traps around existing evidence-labeled examples.
strengths: Can generate controlled hard negatives from public corpora.
risks: Requires review so synthetic conflicts remain realistic.
Must track which documents are original versus benchmark wrappers.

approaches.name: Compose multi-source suites
approaches.description: Pair rows across complementary datasets so an agent must choose between scientific papers, Wikipedia evidence, table evidence, claims, and long-form explanations.
strengths: Exposes source authority and cross-document contradiction.

seed_tasks.question_template: Using only the cited documents, answer the bridge question and name both supporting pages. Do not cite a page unless it supplies one required hop.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The agent answers from one page and cites a second page that is topically related but not required for the inference.

seed_tasks.question_template: Given an older claim document and a newer evidence document, answer as of the newer document date and explicitly mark stale statements.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The agent treats stale evidence as current or blends incompatible snapshots.

seed_tasks.question_template: Answer the paper question after an appended erratum/appendix section changes the method description. Distinguish original-body evidence from appended evidence.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The agent cites the original paper body for a conclusion superseded by the appended section.

seed_tasks.question_template: Compute the answer from a table, then verify that the surrounding text supports the interpretation of the table column.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The agent extracts the correct table cell but draws a conclusion the caption or text does not support.

seed_tasks.question_template: Resolve a conflict between a crowd explanation, a claim page, and an evidence page. Prefer the highest-authority source and explain why.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The agent quotes the clearest prose rather than the most authoritative source.

seed_tasks.question_template: Answer only if the provided evidence establishes the claim. Otherwise abstain and list the missing evidence.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The agent supplies a plausible answer despite unanswerable or not-enough-info labels.

seed_tasks.category: citation supports fact but not conclusion
seed_tasks.question_template: Return an answer only if every conclusion sentence is directly supported by the cited evidence, not merely by a related fact.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The citation supports a premise, but the agent adds an unsupported causal or comparative conclusion.

seed_tasks.question_template: Answer about the requested entity when distractor documents or table rows contain same-name or near-name entities.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The agent merges entities that share a name, title, place, or abbreviation.

seed_tasks.category: temporal questions: as of date X
seed_tasks.question_template: Answer as of a specified date X, treating later documents as unavailable and earlier documents as possibly stale.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The agent leaks future evidence into an as-of answer or ignores the date constraint.

seed_tasks.question_template: Identify whether the documents agree, conflict, or are insufficient; do not collapse contradictory evidence into a single synthesized answer.
seed_tasks.expected_failure: The agent averages or paraphrases conflicting evidence into a false consensus.

metrics.description: Final answer matches the gold answer or correctly abstains.
All required evidence units are cited.
Cited evidence directly supports the answer sentence it is attached to.
The answer detects stale, contradictory, or lower-authority documents instead of blending them.
The answer respects as-of dates and document lifecycle boundaries.
The answer refuses when evidence is insufficient and names what evidence would be needed.
